newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: Human cloning unacceptable, WHO states declare.
newsitem.headline: Human cloning unacceptable, WHO states declare.

text.p: Member governments of the World Health Organisation, in a cautious contribution to international debate on cloning, agreed on Tuesday that the artificial creation of identical humans was "ethically unacceptable and contrary to human integrity and morality".
Their resolution, passed by consensus, is not legally binding and stopped short of calling for an outright ban on human cloning.
The sci-fi fantasy of cloning humans moved closer to reality this year when geneticists in Scotland used a cell from an adult sheep to create another virtually identical adult.

"Developments in cloning and other genetic procedures have unprecedented ethical implications," said the WHO general assembly motion proposed by countries including Britain, Canada, Finland, Germany, Japan, Norway and Sweden..
"Related research and development must be monitored and assessed, and the rights and dignity of patients respected."
